name: Soyuz (11A511)
best_known_for: R-7-derived launcher for the first-generation Soyuz spacecraft — flew Soyuz 1 (1967) and Soyuz 11 (1971)
credit: The Soyuz 11A511 was the R-7 derivative built to loft the first-generation Soyuz 7K-OK spacecraft, adding a more capable upper stage to the Vostok/Voskhod launcher lineage. Three-stage liquid-propellant (LOX + kerosene), ~50 metres tall, ~308 tonnes lift-off mass. It carried the crewed Soyuz programme's earliest flights, including its two fatal missions — Soyuz 1 (1967), lost when its recovery parachutes fouled, and Soyuz 11 (1971), whose crew died of depressurisation during descent. The 11A511 was succeeded by the Soyuz-U in 1973; the same R-7 lineage still flies crews as the Soyuz-2 today.
